# Getting started with Serverless AI jobs: Run nvidia-smi within a job

export const resource_0 = "job"

You can use Serverless AI jobs to work with AI models and perform such operations as fine-tuning, scientific simulations, data processing or batch inference.

To get started with jobs, use the example below. It demonstrates how to run `nvidia-smi` in a Serverless AI job. As a result, you receive information about the GPUs of the [container virtual machine](/compute/virtual-machines/containers) (VM) in which the job is running. In the web console, the **nvidia-smi** quick-start configuration runs the same kind of workload with settings already filled in.

## Prerequisites

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Web console">
    In the [Administration → Limits → Quotas](https://console.nebius.com/quota) section, check the **Number of virtual machines** (VMs) quota under **Compute**: it should have at least one VM available. If necessary, [increase the quota](/overview/quotas#change-quotas).
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="CLI">
    * [Install and configure](/cli/install) the Nebius AI Cloud CLI.

      Check that your project ID is saved in the Nebius AI Cloud CLI profile configuration:

      ```bash theme={null}
      cat ~/.nebius/config.yaml
      ```

    * In the [Administration → Limits → Quotas](https://console.nebius.com/quota) section, check the **Number of virtual machines** (VMs) quota, under **Compute**: it should have at least one VM available. If necessary, [increase the quota](/overview/quotas#change-quotas).
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="REST API">
    * Get an access token to [authenticate to the REST API](/rest-api/authentication).
    * In the [Administration → Limits → Quotas](https://console.nebius.com/quota) section, check the **Number of virtual machines** (VMs) quota, under **Compute**: it should have at least one VM available. If necessary, [increase the quota](/overview/quotas#change-quotas).
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

## Steps

### Run a Serverless AI job

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Web console">
    1. In the sidebar, go to <Icon icon="https://mintcdn.com/nebius-ai-cloud/rOlLZ_MFvrheaI-h/_assets/sidebar/serverless-ai.svg?fit=max&auto=format&n=rOlLZ_MFvrheaI-h&q=85&s=4c90b50c6c33e6bff000b87b8e37765a" width="16" height="16" data-path="_assets/sidebar/serverless-ai.svg" /> **Serverless AI** → **Jobs**.
    2. Select the **nvidia-smi** quick start card.
       The quick start configuration uses a verified container image and prefilled job settings.
    3. Click **Create job**.
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="CLI">
    Use `nebius ai create` to create a {resource_0} step by step in the terminal. The command prompts you to enter values to pass as parameters, shows the resulting configuration and then creates the {resource_0}.

    1. Run the following command:
       ```bash theme={null}
       nebius ai create \
         --type job \
         --name my-job \
         --image nvidia/cuda:13.1.1-runtime-ubuntu24.04 \
         --container-command bash \
         --args "-c nvidia-smi" \
         --platform gpu-l40s-a \
         --preset 1gpu-8vcpu-32gb \
         --timeout 1h
       ```
       Alternatively, you can run `nebius ai create` and specify each value step by step with CLI prompts. The command pre-fills the following values:
       * `--name`: Job name.
       * `--image`: Container image to run. In the given example, the [nvidia/cuda:13.1.1-runtime-ubuntu24.04](https://hub.docker.com/layers/nvidia/cuda/13.1.1-runtime-ubuntu24.04/images/sha256-7ced05425d3bdea47c018551ee001f28081dd409efe1283872cd968ad3c1e957) image is used. It contains the Ubuntu 24.04 operating system as well as drivers and other components for GPUs.
       * `--container-command`: Terminal shell for commands to run.
       * `--args`: Arguments for `docker run` to pass to the entrypoint command. The specified arguments require the container to run `nvidia-smi`.
       * `--platform`: VM platform for the job. As Serverless AI jobs are based on containers over VMs, every job uses [Compute platforms and presets](/compute/virtual-machines/types).
       * `--preset`: Number of GPUs, vCPUs and RAM allocated to the container. The preset must match the selected platform.
       * `--timeout`: Duration after which the job is canceled if it has not completed.
    2. When the CLI prompts you to select a project, region or subnet, select from the values that are available.
    3. Review the resulting configuration, then confirm creation.
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="REST API">
    Send the following request:

    ```bash theme={null}
    curl --request POST \
      --url 'https://api.nebius.cloud/ai/v1/jobs' \
      --header "Authorization: Bearer <access_token>" \
      --header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
      --data '{
        "metadata": {
          "parentId": "<project_ID>",
          "name": "my-job"
        },
        "spec": {
          "image": "nvidia/cuda:13.1.1-runtime-ubuntu24.04",
          "containerCommand": "bash",
          "args": "-c nvidia-smi",
          "platform": "gpu-l40s-a",
          "preset": "1gpu-8vcpu-32gb",
          "timeout": "3600s",
          "subnetId": "<subnet_ID>",
          "disk": {
            "type": "NETWORK_SSD",
            "sizeBytes": 268435456000
          }
        }
      }'

    ```

    In the `Authorization` header, replace `<access_token>` with the access token that you got in the prerequisites.

    The request includes the following parameters:

    * `metadata.parentId`: [Project ID](/iam/manage-projects#how-to-get-a-project-id).
    * `metadata.name`: Job name.
    * `spec.image`: Container image to run. In the given example, the [nvidia/cuda:13.1.1-runtime-ubuntu24.04](https://hub.docker.com/layers/nvidia/cuda/13.1.1-runtime-ubuntu24.04/images/sha256-7ced05425d3bdea47c018551ee001f28081dd409efe1283872cd968ad3c1e957) image is used. It contains the Ubuntu 24.04 operating system as well as drivers and other components for GPUs.
    * `spec.containerCommand`: Terminal shell for commands to run.
    * `spec.args`: Arguments for `docker run` to pass to the entrypoint command. The specified arguments require the container to run `nvidia-smi`.
    * `spec.platform`: VM platform for the job. As Serverless AI jobs are based on containers over VMs, every job uses [Compute platforms and presets](/compute/virtual-machines/types).
    * `spec.preset`: Number of GPUs, vCPUs and RAM allocated to the container. The preset must match the selected platform.
    * `spec.timeout`: Duration after which the job is canceled if it has not completed.
    * `spec.subnetId`: [Subnet ID](/vpc/networking/resources#how-to-get-a-subnet-id).
    * `spec.disk.type`: Disk type for the container over VM.
    * `spec.disk.sizeBytes`: Disk size in bytes. The specified value is 250 GiB.

    The response returns the job ID in the `resourceId` parameter. Save this value because you need it in later steps.
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

The job takes several minutes to complete. While the job is running, you can check its status and logs.

### Check the job status and results

<Note>
  Checking job logs is available only in the web console and CLI.
</Note>

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Web console">
    1. In the sidebar, go to <Icon icon="https://mintcdn.com/nebius-ai-cloud/rOlLZ_MFvrheaI-h/_assets/sidebar/serverless-ai.svg?fit=max&auto=format&n=rOlLZ_MFvrheaI-h&q=85&s=4c90b50c6c33e6bff000b87b8e37765a" width="16" height="16" data-path="_assets/sidebar/serverless-ai.svg" /> **Serverless AI** → **Jobs**.
    2. Next to the job, click **View logs**. Alternatively, select the job that you want to view the logs for and switch to the **Logs** tab.
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="CLI">
    1. Save the job ID to an environment variable:
       ```bash theme={null}
       export JOB_ID=$(nebius ai job get-by-name --name my-job \
         --format jsonpath='{.metadata.id}')
       ```
    2. View information about the job:
       ```bash theme={null}
       nebius ai job get $JOB_ID
       ```
       The command output contains such data as the job status, start and finish times.
    3. If the output doesn't indicate that the job has started, wait a few seconds. Next, run the previous command again and check that the job is running now.
    4. When the job has started, check its logs:
       ```bash theme={null}
       nebius ai job logs $JOB_ID
       ```
       The logs contain information about the GPUs that `nvidia-smi` provides (in other words, the output of the `nvidia-smi` command).

    You can run `nebius ai job get $JOB_ID` and `nebius ai job logs $JOB_ID` multiple times to determine whether the job is complete, and the full output of `nvidia-smi` is returned in logs.
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="REST API">
    Get the job and check the `status.state` parameter in the response:

    ```bash theme={null}
    curl --request GET \
      --url "https://api.nebius.cloud/ai/v1/jobs/<job_ID>" \
      --header "Authorization: Bearer <access_token>"
    ```

    In the request, specify:

    * Your access token in the `Authorization` header.
    * In the request path, the job ID returned in the `resourceId` parameter when you created the job.

    If the state doesn't indicate that the job has started, wait a few seconds and send the request again. You can repeat the request until the job reaches the `COMPLETED` state.
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

### (Optional) Delete the job

When the job is complete, Serverless AI automatically releases all allocated computing resources and the container disk of the job. When you delete a completed job, you remove it from the list of Serverless AI jobs.

If you delete a running job, all the resources are released as well.

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Web console">
    1. In the sidebar, go to <Icon icon="https://mintcdn.com/nebius-ai-cloud/rOlLZ_MFvrheaI-h/_assets/sidebar/serverless-ai.svg?fit=max&auto=format&n=rOlLZ_MFvrheaI-h&q=85&s=4c90b50c6c33e6bff000b87b8e37765a" width="16" height="16" data-path="_assets/sidebar/serverless-ai.svg" /> **Serverless AI** → **Jobs**.
    2. Locate the job and then click <Icon icon="https://mintcdn.com/nebius-ai-cloud/1Ha0sWR6e1mnIaHS/_assets/button-vellipsis.svg?fit=max&auto=format&n=1Ha0sWR6e1mnIaHS&q=85&s=e80b8e57c43bfd117679262e6a1334ad" width="12" height="24" data-path="_assets/button-vellipsis.svg" /> → **Delete**.
    3. In the window that opens, confirm deleting the job.
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="CLI">
    To delete the job, run the following command:

    ```bash theme={null}
    nebius ai job delete $JOB_ID
    ```
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="REST API">
    To delete the job, send the following request:

    ```bash theme={null}
    curl --request DELETE \
      --url "https://api.nebius.cloud/ai/v1/jobs/<job_ID>" \
      --header "Authorization: Bearer <access_token>"
    ```

    In the request, specify:

    * Your access token in the `Authorization` header.
    * In the request path, the job ID returned in the `resourceId` parameter when you created the job.
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

# AGENTS.md — hack-os shared agent instructions

Single source of truth for every coding harness. `CLAUDE.md` points here.
Read this whole file once per session. These rules govern product work;
explicitly requested maintenance of hack-os itself is not constrained by
an example product's demo script or contract.

## 1. Boot sequence and freshness

If `.hackos-user` is absent, run `./bootstrap.sh --auto` once. Bootstrap is
local-only: no downloads, product dependency installs, git config changes,
or credentials. Missing tools warn; markdown remains usable. Identity not
matched to the roster is unconfirmed: ask the human, never assume ownership.
MCP authentication and personal API keys are optional, per-person setup.

Read `team-setup/state/event.json` first. `mode: example`, or a legacy
`_comment` containing `WORKED EXAMPLE` without an explicit mode, means NO
active event. Say "No active event; fictional examples are inactive."
A blank `event_name` also means no active event, regardless of mode; report
"No event configured" and do not load placeholder state as requirements.
Do not load fictional challenges, contracts, owners, tasks, or decisions as
requirements. Never silently initialize or reset an event.
The distributed template keeps event records and shared session logs empty.
Keep the reusable roster in `team.json`; assign product roles fresh per event.

For an active event, read in order:
1. `team-setup/state/pipeline.json`
2. `team-setup/state/decisions.md` — identify current, non-superseded decisions.
3. `team-setup/state/owners.md`
4. `team-setup/board/tasks.json` — identify the relevant task and accountable owner.
5. `team-setup/state/01-challenge-pick/challenge.md`
6. `team-setup/state/02-demo-script/demo-script.md`
7. `team-setup/state/02-demo-script/not-building.md`
8. `team-setup/state/03-contract-freeze/contract.md`
Load `ideas.md`, `research.json`, and supporting notes when relevant.
Any document marked `WORKED EXAMPLE` is illustrative, never active scope.

State the active stage, your confirmed ownership, current task/decisions,
and whether the real contract is frozen. Missing information is unknown,
not permission to invent assignments or implement fictional requirements.

Before a new task or substantial edit, reread decisions, ownership, the
relevant task and contract. After a teammate reports a change, refresh even
in a running session. A dashboard refresh does not refresh an agent's mind.

Git is explicit synchronization, not live collaboration. `event.json`
names the coordination branch and maintainer. The maintainer integrates
accepted state changes there; teammates fetch and safely integrate before
new work and at checkpoints. Never auto-pull into a dirty worktree, discard
changes, auto-stash, or resolve another person's conflicts. Show local HEAD,
uncommitted coordination edits, and remote freshness as unknown until checked.
Offline work uses a local snapshot, never a claimed live team state.

## 2. Hackathon mode

- Write smoke tests for the demo happy path and coordination data safety.
- Do not add unit tests for unrelated product code or refactor working code.
- No speculative abstractions, new dashboards, providers, or services.
- Core storage/API stays Python 3 stdlib plus Git. The dashboard UI uses
  Vite, React, Tailwind and shadcn/ui in `team-setup/board/web/`; its Node
  dependencies are separate from whichever product stack the team chooses.
- Optional MCPs, plugins, prompt logging, and agent teams are not prerequisites.
- Vendored skills are optional; these repository rules override their workflow
  defaults. A skill does not authorize unrequested installs, data uploads,
  extra agents, destructive commands, or changes to system security controls.

## 3. Ownership rule

Before editing, check `team-setup/state/owners.md` and the owning task in
`team-setup/board/tasks.json`. Do not edit another person's assigned files.
A sub-owner helps within an explicitly delegated boundary; they do not
redirect scope. Name owners for shared wiring, manifests and lockfiles too.
Ownership is per event, not inferred from background. Use one branch/worktree
per independent writer; worktrees alone do not sync different machines.
Reassignments and delegation must be explicit and synced before work starts.
Avoid direct file editing while a dashboard write touches the same records.

## 4. Contract rule

The real `team-setup/state/03-contract-freeze/contract.md` freezes when that
gate completes. Code against it and mock missing dependencies. A required
contract change needs explicit human approval and a recorded decision.
`app/shared/` is generated from the agreed contract, never independently
patched. No sample schema, endpoint, or product stack is a requirement.

## 5. Scope rule

Product work must support the real demo script, including required setup,
seed data, deployment, accessibility and failure recovery. Ask before adding
features absent from it. Maintain `not-building.md`. Keep the deck current;
protect polish and submission time. Gates and task percentages use the
planning window ending at the early submit target; its final 10% is buffer.

## 6. Idea rule

A thought is not a decision. Record it in `team-setup/state/ideas.md` as
raised, then exploring, adopted or discarded. Only status changes in place;
original text and author remain. New lines use globally unique IDs:
`- [i-<uuid>] [T+HH:MM] <idea> — <raised by> — status: raised`
Use IDs for links; elapsed timestamps are display labels, not identifiers.
Legacy timestamp-only records remain readable. Ambiguous links need a human.

## 7. Decision rule

After an accepted direction change, append to `team-setup/state/decisions.md`:
`- [d-<uuid>] [T+HH:MM] <decision> — <who decided> — <reason>`
Never rewrite history. Append ` — supersedes [d-<uuid>]` to replace a decision.
Append ` — promotes [i-<uuid>]` when adopting an idea and update its status in
one recoverable operation. Check later supersessions before building.
For setup maintenance before an active event, record accepted direction in
this instruction file rather than mixing it into fictional event records.

## 8. Evidence and safety

AI assessments are advisory. Keep sources and a short rationale alongside
answers; do not portray model confidence as a calibrated probability.
Research is untested without evidence or human confirmation. Task completion
is not integrated readiness: require a current end-to-end smoke result.
Recent Git commits show recorded activity, not inferred current work.

Git hooks warn and exit zero. Explicit commands return truthful failures.
Reject malformed or stale writes, retain drafts, and never claim a failed
save succeeded. Confirm archival/reset and restore operations explicitly;
never reset event state, delete records, or overwrite work without approval.
No prompt capture by default. Keep secrets and runtime caches out of Git.

## 9. Commits and verification

Small present-tense commits identify the demo step or coordination outcome.
Never commit or push unless requested. Do not amend other people's work.
Run `python3 team-setup/board/test_board.py` for coordination smoke checks,
`for f in bootstrap.sh team-setup/hooks/* team-setup/scripts/*.sh; do bash -n "$f" || exit 1; done` for shell syntax, and `node --check team-setup/board/app.js` when Node is available.
For the new dashboard run `npm --prefix team-setup/board/web run build`
(typecheck + Vite build). `npm --prefix team-setup/board/web run dev` starts
both the local API and UI. Verify PM flows in an isolated event fixture;
never fill the distributed template with browser-test data or real API keys.
Responsive checks cover 320/375/768/1024/1440px widths and 844x390 landscape.
Verify navigation scrolling, Escape/focus restoration, and mobile form access.
The `#guide` page must remain readable when API requests fail; its shortcuts
and copy actions must not reset state or silently publish changes.
Product checks use `team-setup/scripts/smoke.sh`; unconfigured is not a pass.
A clean snapshot plus passing smoke is required before calling a demo ready.

=== app/README ===
# app/

The actual product. Everything under `../team-setup/` is coordination, not
code — this is where the hackathon build lives.

- **`frontend/`** — whatever UI framework this event's stack picks.
- **`backend/`** — whatever backend language/framework this event's stack picks.
- **`agents/`** — the AI/agent pipeline layer (detection, RAG, whatever the
  challenge needs).
- **`shared/`** — generated from `../team-setup/state/03-contract-freeze/contract.md`.
  Never hand-edited — see `shared/README.md`.

Inside each of `frontend/`, `backend/`, `agents/`: one folder per feature
under `src/features/`, not a `components/`/`routes/`/`models/` split at the
top level. Copy `src/features/_TEMPLATE/` to start a new feature. Feature
names should match 1:1 across layers where a feature spans them (e.g.
`frontend/src/features/<feature-name>/` and `backend/src/features/<feature-name>/`
are the same feature, two halves).

Who owns which folder is decided fresh per event and lives only in
`../team-setup/state/owners.md` — not here, and not fixed by this template.

## Running everything together

Stack isn't chosen yet in this template, so there's no single command
until the team picks one. Once `frontend/package.json`,
`backend/package.json` (or `pyproject.toml`/`pom.xml`), and
`agents/pyproject.toml` have real dependencies filled in, add the actual
run command here — e.g.:

```bash
# example once a Next.js + FastAPI + Python-agents stack is chosen:
(cd app/frontend && npm run dev) &
(cd app/backend && npm run dev) &
(cd app/agents && python -m agents.main) &
```

`bootstrap.sh` detects whatever is actually in these three folders and
installs dependencies accordingly — it never assumes a stack.

```bash
cd app/backend
npm install && npm run dev     # or: pip install -e . / mvn spring-boot:run,
                                # whichever this event's stack picks
```

Feature folders live in `src/features/`, one per feature, matching
`app/frontend/src/features/` names 1:1 where a feature spans both. Copy
`src/features/_TEMPLATE/` to start a new one.

Owner: see `../../team-setup/state/owners.md` (decided fresh per event,
not fixed here).

## All Job Status Values

| Status | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `STATE_UNSPECIFIED` | "Serverless AI has not classified the status yet." |
| `PROVISIONING` | "The job is creating resources." |

| `DELETING` | "The job is being deleted." |
| `FAILED` | Job failed due to code errors, incorrect config, missing dependencies, or timeout. |
| `ERROR` | "An internal Serverless AI error occurred." |

## Terminal States

Jobs reach completion through these final states:
- **`COMPLETED`** – successful execution
- **`CANCELLED`** – user-initiated cancellation
- **`FAILED`** – workload-related issues (errors, timeouts, bad config)
- **`ERROR`** – platform-level internal failures

## Cancellation & Timeout Behavior

**Cancellation**: Running jobs transition through `RUNNING` → `CANCELLING` → `CANCELLED` when stopped by the user.

```bash

  --service-account-id $SA_ID \
```

"""Example training script for a Nebius Serverless AI job.

Fine-tunes a small causal LM (distilgpt2 by default) on a tiny inline corpus so
the whole run finishes in a few minutes on one L40S. Swap in your own data /
model; keep this file under 64 KiB (it is injected into the container).

(NEBIUS_OUTPUT_VOLUME in .env or --output on the CLI), else to ./out inside
the container disk, which is discarded when the job ends.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import time

import torch


def main() -> None:
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    p.add_argument("--model", default=os.environ.get("MODEL_NAME", "distilgpt2"))
    p.add_argument("--epochs", type=int, default=1)
    p.add_argument("--lr", type=float, default=5e-5)
    p.add_argument("--batch-size", type=int, default=8)
    p.add_argument("--max-steps", type=int, default=50)
    args = p.parse_args()

    out_dir = os.environ.get("NEBIUS_OUTPUT_DIR", "./out")
    os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)
    device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
    print(f"device={device} gpu={torch.cuda.get_device_name(0) if device == 'cuda' else '-'} torch={torch.__version__}", flush=True)

    from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer

    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(args.model)
    tok.pad_token = tok.pad_token or tok.eos_token
    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(args.model).to(device)

    corpus = [
        "Temporal reasoning means ordering events and understanding durations.",
        "A workflow retries a failed activity until it succeeds or times out.",
        "The model learns to predict the next token from context.",
        "Serverless jobs release their GPU when the container exits.",
    ] * 32
    enc = tok(corpus, return_tensors="pt", padding=True, truncation=True, max_length=48)
    ds = torch.utils.data.TensorDataset(enc["input_ids"], enc["attention_mask"])
    dl = torch.utils.data.DataLoader(ds, batch_size=args.batch_size, shuffle=True)

    opt = torch.optim.AdamW(model.parameters(), lr=args.lr)
    model.train()
    step, t0, history = 0, time.time(), []
    for epoch in range(args.epochs):
        for input_ids, attn in dl:
            input_ids, attn = input_ids.to(device), attn.to(device)
            loss = model(input_ids=input_ids, attention_mask=attn, labels=input_ids).loss
            loss.backward()
            opt.step()
            opt.zero_grad()

# Feature: training-jobs

Submit, track, and cancel GPU training runs on **Nebius Serverless AI jobs**
from this backend. A job is a container on a fresh GPU VM: you give it an
image, a command, a platform/preset, and a timeout; Nebius bills the VM while
it runs and releases everything when the container exits.

- `nebius/auth.js`   – access tokens (static token, service-account JWT, or CLI)
- `nebius/client.js` – REST client for `ai/v1/jobs` (+ `iam/v1/profiles`, `vpc/v1/subnets`)
- `nebius/spec.js`   – validated `CreateJobRequest` builder, platform catalog, cost estimate
- `routes/`          – HTTP endpoints under `/api/training/*`
- `cli.js`           – terminal front-end over the same service (`npm run train -- ...`)
- `examples/`        – nvidia-smi check, a distilgpt2 fine-tune, a bring-your-own-image spec

Zero npm dependencies: Node ≥ 22 built-ins only (fetch, crypto, http).

## 1. One-time setup (10 minutes)

### a. Nebius CLI (already installed on this Mac at `~/.nebius/bin/nebius`)

```bash
curl -sSL https://storage.eu-north1.nebius.cloud/cli/install.sh | bash   # if missing
exec -l $SHELL                                                            # picks up PATH
nebius profile create --profile default \
  --endpoint api.nebius.cloud --federation-endpoint auth.nebius.com \
  --parent-id <project_ID>          # opens the browser to log in
nebius profile list                 # sanity check
```

Project ID: **Administration → Projects** in https://console.nebius.com, or
`nebius iam v2 project list --parent-id <tenant_ID>`. It looks like `project-e00…`.

### b. Quota

**Administration → Limits → Quotas → Compute → Number of virtual machines**
must be ≥ 1, and the GPU platform you want (L40S / H100 …) must have a non-zero
quota. Request an increase in the console if not; jobs fail with
`NotEnoughResources` otherwise.

### c. Backend env

```bash
cp app/backend/.env.example app/backend/.env
# set NEBIUS_PROJECT_ID; leave NEBIUS_SUBNET_ID blank for now
cd app/backend && npm run train -- doctor
```

`doctor` authenticates, prints who you are, lists subnets, and tells you the
`NEBIUS_SUBNET_ID` to paste into `.env` if the project has one subnet.

### d. Auth: pick one

| Mode | When | Setup |
|---|---|---|
| CLI profile (default) | laptop, hackathon | nothing beyond `nebius profile create`; the backend shells out to `nebius iam get-access-token` |
| `NEBIUS_ACCESS_TOKEN` | CI, a teammate's machine, 12 h | `nebius iam get-access-token` and paste into `.env` |
| Service account | deployed backend | see below |

Service account (non-interactive, long-lived):

```bash
export SA_ID=$(nebius iam service-account create --name backend-trainer --format jsonpath='{.metadata.id}')
# give it editor rights: Administration → IAM → Groups → editors → add member $SA_ID  (or nebius iam group-membership create ...)
openssl genrsa -out app/backend/secrets/nebius-sa.pem 4096
openssl rsa -in app/backend/secrets/nebius-sa.pem -pubout -out /tmp/nebius-sa.pub.pem
nebius iam auth-public-key create --account-service-account-id $SA_ID --data "$(cat /tmp/nebius-sa.pub.pem)"
# key ID: console → IAM → Service accounts → backend-trainer → Authorized keys
```

Then in `.env`: `NEBIUS_SA_ID`, `NEBIUS_SA_KEY_ID`, `NEBIUS_SA_PRIVATE_KEY_FILE=./secrets/nebius-sa.pem`.
`secrets/` and `*.pem` are git-ignored.

## 2. Run it

### Smoke test (Nebius's own quick start: nvidia-smi on 1× L40S, ~$0.10)

```bash
cd app/backend
npm run train -- smoke
```

Submits, polls every 15 s through `PROVISIONING → STARTING → IMAGE_PULLING →
RUNNING → COMPLETED`, then prints the last 100 log lines (the `nvidia-smi`
table). Takes 3–6 minutes end to end. Exit code 0 means the whole path works.

### Train a script

```bash
npm run train -- submit \
  --name distilgpt2-run1 \
  --script src/features/training-jobs/examples/train.py \
  --requirements src/features/training-jobs/examples/requirements.txt \
  --platform gpu-l40s-a --preset 1gpu-8vcpu-32gb --timeout 1h \
  --env HF_TOKEN=hf_xxx \
  --wait \
  -- --epochs 1 --max-steps 50
```

What happens: the script and requirements are **injected** into the container
at `/workspace/` (limit 64 KiB per file), a generated `run.sh` runs
`pip install -r requirements.txt && python train.py …`, and the job is created.
Without `--wait` the command returns immediately with the job ID.

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--script`, `--requirements` | local files to inject |
| `--platform`, `--preset` | see `npm run train -- catalog` |
| `--timeout` | `1h`…`168h`; the job is killed and billed up to this |
| `--image` | default `pytorch/pytorch:2.7.1-cuda12.8-cudnn9-runtime` |
| `--env K=V` (repeatable) | env vars for the container |
| `--volume SRC:/path[:ro]` (repeatable) | mount a Nebius bucket/filesystem or `s3://bucket` |
| `--output BUCKET` | mount at `/outputs` and set `NEBIUS_OUTPUT_DIR` (or `NEBIUS_OUTPUT_VOLUME` in `.env`) |
| `--preemptible` | cheaper VM that can be killed; only for restartable training |
| `--dry-run` | validate with Nebius without creating anything |
| `-- …` | everything after `--` goes to the script's `sys.argv` |

### Or submit a JSON spec

```bash
npm run train -- submit-spec src/features/training-jobs/examples/finetune-distilgpt2.json --wait
npm run train -- submit-spec src/features/training-jobs/examples/custom-image.json
```

### Track / stop

```bash
npm run train -- list
npm run train -- status <job_id>          # add --raw for the full resource
npm run train -- logs <job_id> --follow   # CLI only: Nebius has no logs REST endpoint
npm run train -- wait <job_id>
npm run train -- cancel <job_id>
npm run train -- delete <job_id>          # removes it from the list; resources are already freed
```

### HTTP API (`npm run dev`, port 8000)

| Method | Path | Body / query |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/api/training/catalog` | platforms, presets, $/GPU-h |
| GET | `/api/training/estimate?platform=&preset=&timeout=2h` | worst-case cost |
| GET | `/api/training/whoami` | auth + project + subnets |
| POST | `/api/training/jobs` | raw job `{name,image,command,args,...}` **or** training job `{name, script, requirements, scriptArgs, env, volumes, platform, preset, timeout}` |
| POST | `/api/training/jobs/dry-run` | same body; validates only |
| GET | `/api/training/jobs` | `?pageSize=&pageToken=` |
| GET | `/api/training/jobs/:id` | `?raw=1` for the full resource |
| GET | `/api/training/jobs/:id/logs` | `?tail=200` (needs the CLI on the server) |
| POST | `/api/training/jobs/:id/cancel` | |
| DELETE | `/api/training/jobs/:id` | |

```bash
curl -s localhost:8000/api/training/jobs -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{
  "name": "api-run-1",
  "script": "import torch; print(torch.cuda.get_device_name(0))",
  "platform": "gpu-l40s-a", "preset": "1gpu-8vcpu-32gb", "timeout": "1h"
}'
```

## 3. Getting data in and models out

- **Small code/config (≤ 64 KiB each):** inject it (`--script`, `--requirements`, `injectedFiles`).
- **Datasets, checkpoints, outputs:** create an Object Storage bucket in the console
  (**Storage → Object Storage → Create bucket**) and mount it: `--volume my-bucket:/data`
  or `--output my-bucket`. The container disk is thrown away when the job ends.
- **Hugging Face Hub:** pass `--env HF_TOKEN=…` and `push_to_hub` from the script.
- **Private images:** `registry: {username, password}` in the JSON spec.

## 4. Budget: what $600 buys (on-demand, Sept 2026 list prices)

| Platform | Preset | $/h | GPU-hours for $600 |
|---|---|---|---|
| gpu-l40s-a | 1gpu-8vcpu-32gb | 1.55 | ~385 |
| gpu-l40s-d | 1gpu-16vcpu-96gb | 1.82 | ~330 |
| gpu-h100-sxm | 1gpu-16vcpu-200gb | 3.85 | ~155 |
| gpu-h200-sxm | 1gpu-16vcpu-200gb | 4.50 | ~133 |
| gpu-h100-sxm | 8gpu-128vcpu-1600gb | 30.80 | ~19 |

Rules of thumb: L40S (48 GB) is fine for ≤ 7B-parameter LoRA/QLoRA and any
small model; go H100/H200 for full fine-tunes or long contexts. **Always set
`--timeout` to what the run should take plus margin**, because a hung job
bills until the timeout. `estimate` prints the worst case before submit.
Also budget for provisioning time (a few minutes per job) and any bucket storage.

## 5. Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Fix |
|---|---|
| `NEBIUS_PROJECT_ID is not set` | copy `.env.example` → `.env` |
| `nebius iam get-access-token` returns nothing | `nebius profile create …`, log in in the browser |
| 403 on create | the account/service account lacks editor on the project |
| `ERROR` / `NotEnoughResources` | GPU quota is 0 or capacity is short: raise the quota or try another platform/preset |
| `FAILED` / `TimeoutExceeded` | raise `--timeout` |
| `FAILED` right after `RUNNING` | `logs <id>`; usually a pip install or script error |
| Preset rejected | run `nebius compute platform list` and use the IDs it prints; the catalog in `spec.js` is a convenience, not the source of truth |
| Logs endpoint returns 501 | install the CLI where the backend runs, or read logs in the console |

## What I built

A `training-jobs` feature under `app/backend/src/features/training-jobs/` that submits, tracks, and cancels GPU jobs on Nebius Serverless AI. It uses only Node built-ins, so there is no `npm install`.

- **`nebius/auth.js`** gets access tokens three ways: a pasted token, a service-account key (RS256 JWT exchange, for a deployed server), or the Nebius CLI.
- **`nebius/client.js`** wraps the REST endpoints I verified against Nebius's OpenAPI spec: create, get, list, cancel, delete, and a poller that waits for a terminal state.

- **`routes/`** exposes it at `/api/training/*`, and `cli.js` gives the same thing in the terminal.

I also installed the Nebius CLI at `~/.nebius/bin`. Job logs are only available through the CLI or console, so the backend shells out to it for logs.

## How to run it

1. Log in once. Type this in the prompt so it runs in your session:
   ```
   ! ~/.nebius/bin/nebius profile create --profile default --endpoint api.nebius.cloud --federation-endpoint auth.nebius.com --parent-id <project_ID>
   ```

2. Check quota. Administration → Limits → Quotas → Compute must allow at least one VM and a non-zero L40S or H100 quota.
3. Configure the backend:
   ```

   ```
4. Smoke test on a real GPU (about ten cents, five minutes):

The feature README covers flags, mounting a bucket for datasets and checkpoints, service-account setup, and troubleshooting.

should i have public or private endpoint ?

Private, which is the default my code uses (`publicIp` is off unless you set it).

**Why private is right for training jobs.** A training job is batch work: it starts, trains, writes outputs to the mounted bucket, and exits. Nothing needs to connect into it. You read logs through the CLI or console, and the container already has outbound internet for pip, Hugging Face downloads, and pushing to the Hub. A public IP adds nothing to that flow. It also uses your public IP quota, costs a little, and exposes the VM to the internet with whatever is listening inside the container.

**When you would want a public endpoint.** Only if you need to reach *into* the job while it runs:

- SSH debugging with `nebius ai job ssh` after adding `sshKeys`.
- Watching TensorBoard or a Jupyter notebook live, with a port declared in the spec.
- Serving a model, which is really a Nebius endpoint rather than a job.

For those cases, set `"publicIp": true` in the JSON spec, or add `publicIp: true` to the API body, and the job's `publicEndpoints` field in `status` will show the address. If a teammate's VM in the same Nebius network needs to reach the job, `privateEndpoints` works without opening it publicly.
